name: Kuwae caldera eruption
summary: Catastrophic caldera collapse in the New Hebrides (Vanuatu) ejects ~30–60 km³ of magma. Tree-ring records from the Northern Hemisphere show severe summer cooling in 1453; the eruption's sulphate signal is the strongest of the 15th century in Greenland and Antarctic ice cores.

_quarry.structural_significance: Major climate-forcing event of the late-medieval Little Ice Age; associated with crop failures in China and the eastern Mediterranean in 1453–1454.
